headline: High: Khoj can read indexed personal notes while the paired content-writing agent has broad network egress, creating default data-leak and downstream misuse risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented between awesome-cli-apps and Khoj, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Khoj reads indexed documents and the other agent is a content-writing tool with broad network egress, so manual copy/paste or pasted document content could still carry instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies Khoj output into the content-writing agent as instructions
IF indexed notes contain attacker-authored text that is later pasted into the other agent
mitigations: Avoid copying raw model output between agents
Strip instructions from pasted notes before reuse
Use a fixed prompt template for the writing agent
Mark untrusted note sources in Khoj
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved chunks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, and its docs show file-based retrieval plus API calls; the other agent has broad network egress. That creates a default pathway where sensitive note content can be surfaced by Khoj and then exfiltrated or reposted by the writing agent. The pair is not proven to share a workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF personal notes or indexed documents contain sensitive data
IF the writing agent is given Khoj outputs that include those notes
mitigations: Limit Khoj indexes to non-sensitive folders
Redact sensitive passages before handoff
Disable broad egress for the writing workflow
Review outputs before external posting
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and public note indexes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write access: awesome-cli-apps has no filesystem or git write capability listed, while Khoj cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Both can use network egress, but that is not a shared mutable resource in the rubric. Conflict risk is therefore limited and mostly absent unless an external orchestrator adds shared writes.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF a shared git workspace is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant filesystem write to the writing agent
Avoid shared git repos for the pair
Use read-only mounts for Khoj indexes
requires-engineering: add lock coordination if shared writes are later enabled

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval-based conversational agent over personal notes, and the writing agent can turn outputs into published content via broad network egress. If the writing agent treats Khoj’s retrieved text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into externalized content. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, not directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the writing agent uses Khoj output without verification
IF retrieved notes are treated as factual source material for publication
mitigations: Require a human fact-check step
Ask Khoj for source citations before reuse
Use a verification checklist before publishing
Limit the writing agent to drafting only
requires-engineering: add citation-aware retrieval and validation

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly handles personal notes and indexed documents, which can include regulated or private data, while the other agent has broad network egress and no documented residency or retention controls. That mismatch can create compliance exposure if sensitive notes are routed into externally posted content. The other agent is cited because its egress is the compliance-relevant sink.
conditions: IF indexed documents include regulated personal data
IF the writing agent sends derived content to external services or public endpoints
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the index
Use a local-only publishing workflow
Document retention and deletion rules
Review outbound destinations before posting
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
